subject: extracting time-frequency information from the spectro function

messages.author: 8b446c107e0878a8
messages.subject: extracting time-frequency information from the spectro function
parts:
Hi,

I have a time series of 13394 samples. When I use the spectro function it returns an object of 26 by 256 time-frequency samples. But when I look at the plot the time component of the spectogram looks much more detailed than just 26 time samples.

Is it possible to have the spectro function return much more time samples? I would like to have it return a time-frequency matrix of 13394 by 256 samples.

Thanks in advance,
  Robert

messages.author: de80047cbc18c87e
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] extracting time-frequency information from the spectro function
parts:
Hello,

13394 samples / 512 = 26 FT windows. As the FT is a mirror function
you end up with 26 windows of 512/2 = 256 points.

If you want to increase the number of windows, use the argument 'ovlp'
that specifies the overlap between successive FT windows in %. For
isntance, a value of 50% will double the number of windows.

HTH

Jerome

messages.author: 0efd2d7533d4b99f
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] extracting time-frequency information from the spectro function
parts:
Hi, it is a non-sense to produce as many fft as the number of samples you have. By managing together the FFT size, the Window size (or the zero-padding parameter) and the overlap you can try to optimize the frequency-time resolution and selectivity according to the structure of your signal and the information you want to get.

Gianni
